tools.name: core-settings-manage
tools.description: Update platform settings (name, host, lang, CORS, logo, favicon, default site, SEO files, backend theme colors). Assets accept URLs only. Never use cors_allow_all in production. The API has no read for account settings: the result is the platform response to the write, compared field by field with what was sent. Theme colors are applied but not returned; a host or lang change returns a redirect instead of the settings, so those fields are reported as not verifiable.

action.description: update=modify. The API has no read for account settings

name.description: Platform name

logo.description: Logo (URL only). null=remove. name excludes extension

name.description: Asset file name

favicon.description: Favicon (URL only). null=remove. name excludes extension

name.description: Asset file name

primary_hover.description: Backend primary hover color in hex

accent_hover.description: Backend accent hover color in hex

page_background.description: Backend page background color in hex

navigation_selected_text.description: Backend navigation selected text color in hex

navigation_selected_background.description: Backend navigation selected background color in hex

verify.description: Inert: the API has no read for account settings; the result is the platform response to the write

tools.name: core-users-bulk
tools.description: Bulk activate/deactivate users. Use list-affected to preview before applying. Priority: user_ids > query/active_filter > all. The platform applies the change in a background job: the response reports how many users were queued (state.status "queued"), not how many changed; read the users afterwards to confirm. Destructive: test in staging first.

all.description: Selects every user in scope; preview with list-affected first

verify.description: Count matching users before and right after queuing (default: false). The job may still be running

tools.name: core-users-upsert
tools.description: Idempotent user create/update by email/username. Create requires all profile fields + password (min 12). Use core-groups-manage for permissions after creation.

tools.name: core-users-manage
tools.description: Manage admin users: create, update, list, sessions, or get current user (me). New users get the default account_user role; grant access to a site, space or realm with core-members-manage. Every write returns the user read back afterwards. Activating or deactivating is asynchronous on the platform: the tool reads the user again once after a short wait if the change is not visible yet. role_id must be an account role. Removing the two-factor authentication of another admin is not available through the API.

identifier.description: Email, username, or ID (req for manage/sessions)

username.description: Username for create. Defaults to the email when omitted

password.description: Password (required for create, min 12 chars). The platform has no invitation flow without one

send_password.description: Create: email the password to the new user (default: false)

role_id.description: Account role ID (use core-roles-manage context=account to list)

confirmed.description: Removed.

verify.description: Inert: re-reading after manage is always on since 0.5.2; kept for compatibility

tools.name: core-members-manage
tools.description: Assign/update/remove users and groups to sites, spaces, and realms, and list them with their roleship id and role. Use core-roles-manage context=<contextType> for role IDs. Full names NOT reliably resolved as memberId. Writes return the membership read back afterwards. Deactivated admins do not appear in the members list, so they cannot be updated or removed until reactivated.

action.description: add, update (role), remove, or list members

contextId.description: Context identifier: ID, slug, or name

memberId.description: ID, email/username, or group name. Req for add/update/remove

memberType.description: user or group. Req for add/update/remove

roleId.description: ID or key (e.g. 'site_editor'). Req for add/update

confirmed.description: Pass true to run the deletion. Without it, on clients that do not support interactive confirmation, the tool describes what it would delete and runs nothing.

tools.name: content-spaces-copy
tools.description: Clone entire space with types, categories (with their hierarchy), entries (each translation in its locale, as drafts) and assets. Auto-suffixes UID on conflict. If any category, type or entry is not copied completely, the call fails with COPY_COUNT_MISMATCH and the details; the target space is kept. Large copies run async (check with content-jobs-manage).

sourceSpaceId.description: Source space ID, UID, or name

newName.description: Name of the new space. Space names are unique in the account, so it must differ from the source name.

copyEntries.description: Copy all entries with their translations (default: false). Entries are created as drafts: published and archived states are not copied.

entryLimit.description: Max entries per type (for testing); each entry is copied with all its translations

includeDetails.description: true = full details; false = minimal fields

tools.description: Content space lifecycle. Smart identifier resolution (ID, UID, or name). delete queues the removal in a background job: the response is "queued", and the space stops being returned once the job finishes.

name.description: Required for create

uid.description: Required for create; immutable after creation

locales.description: Locale codes from the platform locale list, e.g. ['es', 'en', 'es-cl', 'pt-br']

The validator picks its rule profile from widget.manifest.json: domain-1.4 for a widget created from the template 1.4 or a later 1.x, type-based when there is no manifest; an unsupported manifest fails closed (profile null, with an error). projectPath.description: Absolute path to the widget project on the MCP server's filesystem. Preferred for local hooks that pass paths directly. Mutually exclusive with projectFiles.

projectFiles.description: Array of virtual files representing the widget — each item is { path, content }. Preferred for portable, cross-client invocation when the MCP server cannot read from the client's filesystem. Mutually exclusive with projectPath. Include widget.manifest.json: the validator picks its rule profile from it. Virtual files cannot represent an empty directory, so an empty directory does not exist for the rules. A widget created from the template is not affected.

path.description: Path relative to the widget root.

allowLegacyStack.description: Bypass the stack-alignment check against WIDGETS_COMPAT. Set to true only when intentionally validating a widget on a legacy Dynamic UI stack. The validator will still run all universal rules; only the major-version mismatch issue added by the MCP wrapper will be suppressed.

instructions:
Unified MCP Server for Modyo Platform


## Modyo MCP Server

Unified server for Modyo platform: Core, Content, Channels, Customers, Widgets.

### Key Rules

**IDs & Stability**: Widget/Template/Entry IDs change after publishing — always use UUIDs for stable references. Bulk operations are async.
**Security**: Inline styles/scripts require `nonce="{{csp_nonce}}"`. Links must use `{{ site.url }}` prefix (never bare `/path`).
**Permissions**: New admin users get the default `account_user` role and must be added as members of each site, space or realm they need — use `core-members-manage`. Groups assign a role in a context to several users at once.

### Workflows
- **Content**: Create space → Define types → Create entries → Publish. Entry states: draft, in review (when the space has team review), published, scheduled, archived. Unpublishing returns an entry to draft.
- **Channels**: Create site → Define pages → Add widgets → Publish. Widget dev: Create definition → Add code → Publish → Add to page.
- **Customers**: Create realm → Add users → Set up forms. Originations: Create → Add steps → Add questions → Publish.

### Channels — Templates & Design

**Template categories**: `layout` (page wrapper with `{{ content_for_layout }}`), `custom_snippet` (reusable via `{% snippet 'name' %}`), `system_snippet` (built-in head/header/footer — editable, NOT deletable), `stylesheet`/`javascript` (static CDN assets).

**System snippets**: ALWAYS customize `header`/`footer` via `channels-templates-upsert` with `category: "system_snippet"`. NEVER create custom_snippets for the same purpose.

**Snippet naming convention**: Use `_css` or `_js` suffix when snippet content is exclusively CSS or JavaScript (e.g. `my_widget_css`, `analytics_js`). For HTML/Liquid snippets — including system_snippets like `header`, `footer`, `head` — use no suffix.

**Layout HTML structure**: Use `{% html5 %}/{% endhtml5 %}` and `{% body %}/{% endbody %}` block tags — NEVER `{{ html5.open_tag }}`/`{{ html5.close_tag }}`. Include `{% snippet 'shared/general/body_tag_manager' %}` right after `{% body %}`.

**Snippet path derivation**: To reference a snippet via `{% snippet 'path' %}`, derive the path from the template's `path` field (from `channels-templates-find`): (1) remove the `site/` prefix, (2) remove the leading `_` and `.html.liquid` suffix from the filename. Example: `site/shared/general/_head.html.liquid` → `shared/general/head`. NEVER guess snippet paths.

**CSS token-first approach**: Read `root.css` first (Bootstrap design tokens). Override `-rgb` tokens only (`--bs-primary-rgb`, etc.). Use `base.css` for custom rules. Never use hex values directly — use `rgb(var(--bs-*-rgb))`. Prefer Bootstrap utility classes in HTML.

**CSS inclusion**: Stylesheet templates (`root.css`, `base.css`) are static CDN assets — include them in the `head` system_snippet via `{{ 'root' | asset_url: 'css' | stylesheet_tag: media: 'screen', nonce: csp_nonce }}`. NEVER use `{% stylesheet 'name' %}` in layouts — that tag does not exist in Modyo Liquid.

**New site structure**: A freshly created site already has a home page (type `home_layout_page`, path `''`) and an about page (path `'about'`), system_snippets (`head`, `header`, `footer`, etc.), and empty `root.css`/`base.css`. Customize them — do NOT recreate. New widget pages auto-use `site/base` layout; update to custom layout via `channels-pages-widget layout` param.

### Channels — Page Content Strategy

- **Widget Definitions**: Interactive components, business logic, JS, or reusable across pages. Create → publish → reference via `nameOrUuid`.
- **Content Pages**: Pages that primarily display entries from a content type (listings, indexes).
- **HTML Blocks**: Simple static content only (banners, CTAs). <30 lines; if larger, use a widget.

### Channels — Liquid Quick Reference

**Navigation**: `{% assign items = menus['slug'].items | visible_items %}{% for item in items %}` → `item.label`, `item.url`, `item.child_items` (filter children too: `item.child_items | visible_items`). `visible_items` is a filter, not a menu property.
**Session**: `{% if user %}` (NOT `user.logged_in`). Props: `user.name`, `user.email`, `user.avatar.url`. URLs: `{{ site.url }}/login`, `{{ site.url }}/logout`.
**Search**: `<form action="{{ site.url }}/search" method="get"><input name="query"></form>`

**Links**: [Docs](https://docs.modyo.com) · [Core](https://docs.modyo.com/en/platform/core/) · [Content](https://docs.modyo.com/en/platform/content/) · [Channels](https://docs.modyo.com/en/platform/channels/) · [Customers](https://docs.modyo.com/en/platform/customers/)

### Widgets

To generate transactional widgets (React + Dynamic UI), the operator initializes the base project with `/mcp__modyo__widgets-init-project` (the `widgets-init-project` Prompt instructs invoking the `widgets-scaffold` Tool, which clones the canonical template at the tag pinned by the compatibility matrix). Two-step flow: first the scaffold, then the operator provides the functional description — do not write widget code before receiving it. Once initialized, read [`modyo://docs/widgets/INDEX`](modyo://docs/widgets/INDEX) for critical rules, patterns and workflow. The tools `widgets-list-components`, `widgets-get-component-props`, `widgets-list-patterns` federate the catalog of Dynamic UI's deployed Storybook; `widgets-validate` runs the validator (package `@modyo/widget-validator`) on a local or virtual widget and returns a `ValidationReport`. The optional Claude Code integration (`PostToolUse` hook for the validator) lives in [`modyo://docs/widgets/_meta-integration-claude-code`](modyo://docs/widgets/_meta-integration-claude-code).

**Catalog Resources** (read on demand, backed by versioned Storybook manifests):
- `modyo://widgets/catalog/components` — lightweight list (id, name, key, description, storyCount)
- `modyo://widgets/catalog/components/{componentId}` — full detail (stories with snippet code, props with TypeScript types, JSDoc tags)
- `modyo://widgets/catalog/patterns` — lightweight pattern list (id, name, title)
- `modyo://widgets/catalog/patterns/{patternId}` — full MDX content of a pattern story

These Resources serve official Storybook manifests from the versioned CDN. They provide richer data (story snippet code, MDX docs) than the legacy `widgets-list-*` tools. See the Pattern Discovery section below for when consultation is required.

### Pattern Discovery (REQUIRED before generating widget UI)

Before writing TSX for the widget's UI, you MUST query the catalog for an official pattern matching the domain of the request:

1. **List patterns**: read `modyo://widgets/catalog/patterns`.
2. **Identify candidates** by matching the request domain against pattern titles and ids (e.g. "transaction history" → `patterns-list-group--transaction-history`).
3. **If a candidate exists**: read `modyo://widgets/catalog/patterns/{patternId}` and use the MDX content as the structural and visual basis for the widget. Adapt to the request's specifics (data shape, locale, domain language) but PRESERVE the layout decisions, component composition, and styling conventions from the pattern.
4. **If no candidate exists**: state explicitly in the response that no official pattern matches, then proceed using only components from `modyo://widgets/catalog/components`.

Why this matters: Dynamic UI patterns embed visual decisions, density, component composition, and styling conventions that are not derivable from component props alone. Skipping this step produces widgets that are technically correct but visually generic — failing to reflect the Dynamic Framework design system.

This step is NOT optional even when the request seems simple. Patterns exist for common use cases (list views, detail panels, forms, dashboards) and apply more often than not.

### Deploy (outside the MCP)

When validation passes (widgets-validate returns passing: true), the widget is done from the MCP's perspective. Deployment runs through CI from the widget's own git repository (the scaffold initializes the repository, and creates the initial commit only when git `user.name` and `user.email` are configured). A manual push is the developer's explicit `modyo-cli push` in their own shell — the agent NEVER runs it.

NEVER include the user's `MODYO_TOKEN` or any credential value in the conversation. Do not read `MODYO_TOKEN` or the widget's `.env`/`.modyo` files into your own context, do not call the Modyo CLI or admin API with the token, and do not echo token material in the chat.
